reason: B provides the clearer, more physically grounded and testable mechanism: a slip-to-twinning transition in low-SFE FCC FeNiCrMn, evaluated against a defined ambient/quasi-static baseline by a controlled temperature–strain-rate matrix and quantitative twin-density measurements. Its main weakness is that twinning may not govern the highest-rate regime, where the cited phonon-drag evidence offers a competing mechanism, but it remains more specific and decisive than A’s vague critical-defect-density/deformation-band proposal.
